title: Europe remains in driver's seat
gist: Global gold ETFs took in US$2.7bn in October 2026 (fourth straight month), lifting holdings 19t to a record 4,275t even as AUM fell 6% to US$542bn on a lower gold price; Europe (US$1.8bn, 18 straight weeks of inflows) and Asia (US$1.3bn, led by China) drove demand while US funds lost US$512mn as investors raised liquidity amid an AI-capex-driven tech sell-off and rotated into Treasuries. Trading volumes fell 13% to US$365bn/day and COMEX net longs dropped 94t to 560t, the lowest since end-July.

themes.theme: Global gold ETF flows: steady inflows despite price dip

insights.claim: Global physically-backed gold ETFs attracted US$2.7bn of inflows in October 2026, their fourth consecutive month of expansion, with European funds leading, Asia net buyers and North America seeing marginal outflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Investor demand for gold ETFs is holding up through a price pullback, suggesting dip absorption rather than capitulation.
insights.quote: Global physically-backed gold ETFs1 attracted US$2.7bn in October, having expanded for four consecutive months

insights.claim: Global gold ETF holdings rose 19t to a month-end record 4,275t in October 2026, while assets under management fell 6% to US$542bn because the lower gold price overshadowed the inflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Tonnage, not AUM, is the cleaner signal of investor appetite; falling AUM here masks rising physical holdings.
insights.quote: Global gold ETFs’ collective holdings climbed 19t to 4,275t, another month-end record.

insights.claim: In the first ten months of 2026 global gold ETFs added US$41bn, the third strongest on record, with holdings up 246t; Europe accounted for 44% and Asia 45% of net inflows, and the UK and China were the largest country contributors.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: 2026 ETF demand leadership has shifted away from North America toward the UK and China.
insights.quote: During the first ten months of the year, global gold ETFs added US$41bn, the third strongest on record

themes.theme: North America: gold as a liquidity source amid AI-driven tech sell-off

insights.claim: North American gold ETFs saw US$512mn of outflows in October 2026, the only region with outflows, driven entirely by US-domiciled funds while Canadian funds kept attracting inflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: US-specific outflows point to domestic cross-asset stress rather than a broad loss of interest in gold.
insights.quote: North American funds saw modest outflows of US$512mn, the only region with outflows in October.

insights.claim: Selling pressure on US technology equities in October 2026, amid growing concerns around AI-related capital spending, may have pushed some investors to sell gold ETF holdings as a ready source of liquidity.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: AI-capex worries are now a cross-asset driver; in acute equity stress gold can be sold first for cash, temporarily hurting flows.
insights.quote: US technology equities came under selling pressure during October amid growing concerns around AI-related capital spend.

insights.claim: The author frames gold's deep liquidity as a key attribute that lets investors meet cash needs during market turbulence, recasting outflows during stress as a feature rather than a weakness.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Short-term gold outflows during equity drawdowns should not be read as a bearish thesis change.

insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Treasuries are competing with gold for safe-haven flows again when yields are elevated and Fed expectations soften.
insights.quote: October saw their strongest monthly return since December 2023 and pulled yields down from the highest in nearly 25 years.

insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Underlying US strategic demand may be intact beneath the headline monthly outflow.

themes.theme: Europe: strategic gold demand on political and fiscal stress

insights.claim: European gold ETFs added US$1.8bn in October 2026, a fourth straight month of inflows, led by the UK with Germany, Switzerland and France also positive, and the region has logged net inflows for 18 consecutive weeks.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Persistent weekly inflows make Europe the marginal driver of ETF gold demand.
insights.quote: the region has experienced net inflows for 18 consecutive weeks

insights.claim: European gold ETF inflows have persisted despite gold price weakness, surging regional yields and shifting central bank expectations, suggesting demand is increasingly strategic rather than driven by opportunity cost or momentum.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Demand that ignores rising yields is stickier and less sensitive to rate repricing.
insights.quote: This suggests that demand for gold ETFs may be increasingly strategic
insights.locator: This is a trend that has persisted

insights.claim: Country-level drivers of European gold demand include social unrest, political fragmentation and difficult fiscal consolidation in France; elevated yields, energy shocks and fiscal headroom narrowed to £11bn in the UK; and weakening momentum plus coalition pressure in Germany.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: European sovereign and political risk is translating directly into gold allocations.
insights.quote: In the UK, elevated yields, energy shocks and shrinking fiscal headroom also sparked concerns.

insights.claim: European investors are turning to gold ETFs for diversification partly because traditional safe-haven government bond markets face their own challenges.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold is gaining share of the safe-haven role as sovereign bonds lose their reliability in Europe.
insights.quote: particularly as traditional safe-haven bond markets face their own challenges

themes.theme: Asia and other regions: falling yields lower gold's opportunity cost

insights.claim: Asian gold ETFs bought US$1.3bn in October 2026, a fourth consecutive month of inflows, led by China, where allocation is linked to the equity market rout and falling government bond yields that reduce the opportunity cost of holding gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Chinese ETF demand is driven by domestic asset weakness and low yields, making it relatively insensitive to gold price dips.
insights.quote: falling government bond yields, which reduce the opportunity cost of holding gold despite the gold price weakness

insights.claim: Japanese gold ETFs drew inflows in October 2026 as the Nikkei pulled back and JGB yields fell on safe-haven flows and softer BoJ tightening expectations, with the BoJ leaving rates unchanged in late October.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A dovish-leaning BoJ supports Japanese gold demand.

insights.claim: India saw sustained gold ETF buying in October 2026 despite local mutual funds temporarily suspending fresh subscriptions to gold fund of funds in mid-October, while other regions added US$62mn on demand from Australia and South Africa.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian demand is strong enough to overcome product-level supply frictions.
insights.quote: India also saw sustained gold ETF buying in the month despite local mutual funds’ temporary suspension

themes.theme: Trading volumes and COMEX positioning cool

insights.claim: Global gold market volumes fell 13% in October 2026 to an average US$365bn per day; OTC dipped 2% to US$219bn/day with LBMA at US$196bn/day, well above the 2025 average of US$161bn/day, while exchange-traded volume fell 25% to US$140bn/day led by a 22% drop at COMEX and a 31% retreat in Shanghai.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The cooling is concentrated in speculative exchange-traded derivatives, while core OTC liquidity remains elevated.
insights.quote: Exchange-traded activity fell the most, shedding 25% in the month to US$140bn/day

insights.claim: Global gold ETF trading liquidity averaged US$6bn/day in October 2026, down 20% month on month, with North America accounting for the lion's share.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: ETF trading activity is fading alongside futures, signaling lower tactical engagement.
insights.quote: Liquidity of global gold ETFs averaged US$6bn/day in the month, a 20% m/m fall

insights.claim: Total COMEX gold net longs fell 94t in October 2026 to 560t, the lowest since end-July, with managed money cutting 53t, other reportables 54t and spreads 13t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Speculative positioning has been cleaned out, reducing downside pressure from forced long liquidation.
insights.quote: Total COMEX net longs fell further, shedding 94t in October to 560t, the lowest since end-July.

insights.claim: Net open interest in COMEX gold options rose 6% in October 2026 and kept climbing in the final days of the month despite the equity sell-off, possibly reflecting rollovers around contract expiry and potential dip buying.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rising options sentiment against falling futures longs hints at early dip-buying interest.
